springs or origins from which water or anything else comes

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the novelist H G Wells, and boreholes as supplies or origins of water.

clue.text: What Pliny wrote needs some translating

explanation.definitionFit: Pliny the Elder and Younger were Romans who composed their works in the classical language of Rome.

clue.text: Aloysius's roommate's quarters forbid drinking wine

clue.text: Raymond Carver collection about the fat revolutionary

explanation.definitionFit: Bach harmonised many Lutheran hymn tunes, so a hymn setting is a typical example of his work, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Grass trilogy's first American hit

explanation.surface: An extract from a song lyric.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical verse, an epode is a lyric piece in which a long line is followed by a shorter one, as in Horace's Epodes.

clue.text: Who hid Bertha somewhere in Kent?

definitions.meaning: the master of Thornfield in Jane Eyre, who kept his mad wife Bertha locked in the attic
a cathedral city on the Medway in Kent, south-east England

explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Brontë's hero shares his name with a town in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Commentator's tip for scorer

explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes scores, and Liszt was a prolific nineteenth-century composer.

clue.text: With school returning, reserves places to write

clue.text: Underworld's premier among ogres

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: the Roman god of the dead is the underworld's chief, and his name gave us words for ogres.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcus was the Roman god ruling the land of the dead, and the source of the word ogre.

clue.text: Kes creator is brilliant? Not initially

explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire novelist Barry Hines wrote the book on which the film Kes was based.

clue.text: McEwan's work agreed time for chaps to visit

ire is anger

explanation.definitionFit: Lestat de Lioncourt is the undead blood-drinker of Anne Rice's novels.

clue.text: Direct aim shot Orestes for one

clue.text: Moving quote about family coming first

clue.text: One beautiful Russian's awfully cold inside

explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus was the youth of Greek myth so handsome he fell in love with his reflection.

clue.text: Slim Pl's visit to a country, cut short

explanation.definitionFit: Peter Cheyney's tough private detective of 1930s fiction is named Slim Callaghan.

clue.text: Followers backed English joiner?

parts.note: a uniter is one who joins things

clue.text: Poem we finally bung on audiotape

clue.text: Like sisters very vocal about Lear in the end

clue.text: Move back and forward in an exacting role

clue.text: Sounding pastoral, he told of good companions

clue.text: Athenian sage's endless farewell

clue.text: Spirit in the Sky — on the radio

clue.text: Legend recited by crude diarist

clue.text: Nobel laureate writer who collected art to burn
